x1dgjt6t.author: Plato
x1dgjt6t.label: Paideia is the art of turning the soul
x1dgjt6t.translation: certain professors of education must be wrong when they say that they can put a knowledge into the soul which was not there before, like sight into blind eyes. ... Whereas, our argument shows that the power and capacity of learning exists in the soul already; and that just as the eye was unable to turn from darkness to light without the whole body, so too the instrument of knowledge can only by the movement of the whole soul be turned from the world of becoming into that of being, ... And must there not be some art which will effect conversion in the easiest and quickest manner; not implanting the faculty of sight, for that exists already, but has been turned in the wrong direction, and is looking away from the truth?
x1dgjt6t.reading: Education does not insert knowledge, as if putting sight into blind eyes; the soul already has the power to see and only needs to be turned toward the light. For her this is the true definition of παιδεία, and the change of seeing (θέασις) leads to θέωσις, awakening and eudaimonia.

xujonsx.author: Parmenides of Elea
xujonsx.label: What is, is ungenerated and all at once
xujonsx.translation: One path only is left for us to speak of, namely, that It is. In it are very many tokens that what is is uncreated and indestructible; for it is complete, immovable, and without end. Nor was it ever, nor will it be; for now it is, all at once, a continuous one.

xujonsx.reading: Only what always is, is; non-being never was. For the ancients "is not" means "is not true": whatever rises and sets, bodies, thoughts, war and peace, booms and busts, has the quality of non-being, which is why our world of experience "seems but is not".

x15q0xms.author: Plato
x15q0xms.label: States grow out of human characters
x15q0xms.translation: Do you know, I said, that governments vary as the dispositions of men vary, and that there must be as many of the one as there are of the other? For we cannot suppose that States are made of 'oak and rock,' and not out of the human natures which are in them, and which in a figure turn the scale and draw other things after them? Yes, he said, the States are as the men are; they grow out of human characters.
x15q0xms.reading: This is the root of her term ψυχοπολιτική, psycho-politics: the polis is the outer reflection of the citizen's soul, so when the soul changes the regime changes. She applies it to what she calls modern Greece's psycho-political trauma.
